**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §2.3. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

For small planning systems, elimination is a systematic method. The same operations appear in numerical solvers and in normal equations for regression, but naive elimination can become unstable when a pivot is close to zero.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
[A\mid b]\ \xrightarrow{\text{row operations}}\ [I\mid x]
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

For u+2v=7 and 2u+v=8, subtract twice the first row from the second to obtain -3v=-6. Thus v=2, then u=3. Swapping rows when a pivot is nearly zero is partial pivoting.

## What follows, and what does not

Row operations preserve the solution set. A zero pivot can indicate singularity or a poor pivot choice. For serious least-squares problems, QR or SVD is usually numerically preferable to forming X^T X.

## Test your reasoning

What happens if the second equation is exactly twice the first, including its right-hand side?
